outcome: maternal SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels (NCP and spike protein IgG)
umbilical cord blood SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels (NCP and spike protein IgG)
maternal TORCH IgG and IgM antibody levels
umbilical cord blood TORCH IgG and IgM antibody levels
cohort: The study included 136 pregnant women between March 2022 and February 2024.
finding: The study demonstrated that maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination resulted in the formation and transplacental transfer of specific antibodies to the unborn child, with no observed differences in pregnancy outcomes, though maternal IgG against spike protein negatively correlated with TORCH antibodies.
